scope: Filament 5.x page-level schema and form composition plus ordinary field presentation

selection_signals: ordinary fields need labels, expected-value guidance, and clear state feedback
long and short values need different spans without losing a logical reading order
related controls may share one composed unit when their values are interpreted together
avoid_when: the problem is primarily page-level grouping, sequencing, or navigation
supporting information applies to a whole workflow rather than one field or immediate task context
responsive_considerations: start with a readable one-column field flow, then let related short fields share rows at wider breakpoints
give long free-form values and error-prone fields a wider or full span rather than equal columns
return fused groups, inline labels, and field guidance to a readable stacked arrangement before their labels, values, or messages collide
accessibility_considerations: labels identify fields and remain visible unless an accessible hidden-label treatment is necessary
required state, validation feedback, disabled state, and focus must remain perceivable without relying only on color
place concise field-level guidance close to the control it qualifies and keep it distinct from the field label
retain a logical keyboard and reading order when fields share a row, fuse, or use inline labels

prefer_when: the label, input, and any feedback need the familiar vertical reading order
avoid_when: the form is a known dense, repetitive set whose short labels and values remain easy to scan inline

prefer_when: a dense, familiar form has short stable labels and vertical space is genuinely constrained
avoid_when: labels, instructions, validation, or long values need the full line to remain scannable

prefer_when: a concise instruction, example, unit, or consequence directly qualifies one field
avoid_when: the text merely repeats the label or explains a broader workflow, policy, or risk

prefer_when: an empty input benefits from a short, realistic example of its expected value
avoid_when: the text would replace the label, required state, instructions, or validation feedback

prefer_when: an immediate field-specific action or component helps complete, verify, or understand that field
avoid_when: the action or information applies to multiple fields or the workflow and belongs in contextual guidance instead

prefer_when: the field is unavailable or requires immediate correction and its reason or feedback can be made clear
avoid_when: a disabled control hides the reason, removes needed recovery, or relies on color alone to communicate the state

prefer_when: two or more values form one compact concept, such as location or a measured value with a unit
avoid_when: the controls are independently understood, require separate guidance or errors, or would become unreadable on narrow screens

prefer_when: a fused concept contains parts with deliberately different expected widths at a wider breakpoint
avoid_when: custom spans only make the row look balanced instead of reflecting value length or importance

prefer_when: a prefix or suffix is part of how the value is read, such as a URL scheme, currency, or unit
avoid_when: the content is optional guidance, an unrelated action, or broad context rather than part of the value

prefer_when: important context, a warning, or a next step affects a group or workflow rather than one field
avoid_when: a short field-specific instruction would be clearer as nearby field-level guidance

selection_signals: one short, self-explanatory group
a container would add visual weight without clarifying hierarchy
avoid_when: groups need names, descriptions, or separate actions
field order or width needs stronger structure
responsive_considerations: keep a readable single-column default
add structure before controls become visually ambiguous
accessibility_considerations: retain visible labels and programmatic grouping when controls form one concept
do not use visual proximity as the only relationship cue

selection_signals: ordinary short related fields can share a row
long fields need space for their expected value
short high-importance fields need a deliberately prominent span
field value lengths differ
avoid_when: a narrow viewport makes multiple columns unreadable
equal widths obscure information hierarchy
responsive_considerations: define one column before larger breakpoints
give long, high-importance fields a deliberate full or wider span
accessibility_considerations: preserve a logical DOM and keyboard order when changing visual spans
never rely on column position to communicate requiredness or sequence

selection_signals: two to four named groups scan top to bottom
descriptions clarify hierarchy
avoid_when: grouping adds no hierarchy
users usually work in one of several large groups
responsive_considerations: collapse columns before reducing field readability
use compact or secondary treatment only when hierarchy remains clear
accessibility_considerations: use headings and descriptions that identify each group
do not collapse essential content by default

prefer_when: a named group needs a visible boundary
avoid_when: the surrounding composition already provides the boundary

prefer_when: a supporting group is intentionally lower in the information hierarchy
avoid_when: the group carries primary task completion

prefer_when: a familiar, low-risk group needs modest density without removing its hierarchy
avoid_when: help, errors, or touch targets need the default breathing room

selection_signals: a group heading and description deserve a separate scan lane
the panel has enough width for context beside controls
avoid_when: the description is too short to earn a separate lane
narrow layouts would crowd labels and inputs
responsive_considerations: return heading and controls to a readable vertical flow on narrow screens
accessibility_considerations: associate descriptions with their group rather than encoding meaning only in side-by-side placement
keep heading order logical when the layout stacks

selection_signals: a small subgroup has a shared label
a visible boundary clarifies a semantic relationship
avoid_when: the border is purely decorative
larger groups need descriptions, actions, or stronger hierarchy
responsive_considerations: keep the group readable at one column before adding internal columns
accessibility_considerations: use the fieldset legend as the group name
ensure the visible boundary reinforces rather than replaces the programmatic group

prefer_when: a visible border helps separate the subgroup from surrounding controls
avoid_when: the boundary would duplicate a containing section

prefer_when: a parent section already makes the subgroup boundary clear
avoid_when: the subgroup would otherwise blend with unrelated controls

selection_signals: a small number of short group labels
frequent switching between parallel groups
avoid_when: content must be compared together
labels overflow available width
input is sequential
responsive_considerations: test label overflow and the overflow menu on narrow screens
do not hide always-needed content behind a non-default tab
accessibility_considerations: keep keyboard tab navigation and focus management intact
make the active panel and tab relationship perceivable

prefer_when: the tab set needs a distinct boundary from surrounding content
avoid_when: a surrounding section already provides that boundary

prefer_when: the parent composition supplies the needed hierarchy and container chrome would be redundant
avoid_when: the active panel would lose a clear visual relationship to its tabs

prefer_when: parallel groups remain valid but labels exceed the available horizontal space
avoid_when: hidden labels would make essential groups hard to discover

selection_signals: several stable groups
sufficient horizontal space
navigation labels benefit from persistent scanning
avoid_when: input is a required sequence
available width is too narrow for a useful navigation rail
responsive_considerations: verify navigation labels remain usable at narrow widths
keep fields within each tab responsive through columns and spans
accessibility_considerations: preserve keyboard navigation between the tab list and panels
do not make the navigation rail the only cue for the active group

selection_signals: later input depends on earlier choices
completion benefits from an explicit ordered path
avoid_when: users need to complete groups in any order
the steps only partition parallel content
responsive_considerations: keep step labels concise and ensure navigation controls remain reachable on narrow screens
accessibility_considerations: communicate current step and completion state programmatically
do not prevent correction of earlier steps without a clear recovery path

selection_signals: each item contains related fields that need a native hierarchy
people need to add, remove, duplicate, or reorder items
a collection is easier to scan through item labels, numbers, or block names
avoid_when: the user is entering one scalar value
a table would hide essential help, errors, or per-item actions
custom cards are proposed only to simulate native repeater or builder hierarchy
responsive_considerations: stack item-internal fields before labels, errors, or actions crowd
prefer button-based reordering when drag handles are hard to use or space is constrained
use the table layout only while every column remains readable and actionable
accessibility_considerations: give each item a distinguishable visible label, number, or block heading
keep add, remove, duplicate, collapse, and reorder actions named and keyboard reachable
keep errors associated with the affected item and field rather than relying on position alone

prefer_when: items are short, uniform rows with stable, scannable columns
avoid_when: an item needs rich guidance, previews, nested fields, or errors that a row would compress

prefer_when: the collection needs an explicit add affordance placed near the items it creates
avoid_when: a distant or generic page action would obscure which collection receives the new item

prefer_when: the order matters and explicit move controls are more discoverable or accessible than dragging
avoid_when: the collection is not ordered

prefer_when: many completed items need compact scanning while their labels still identify them
avoid_when: the current task requires comparing or correcting several item fields together

prefer_when: the collection contains heterogeneous content blocks with meaningful block types
avoid_when: all items share one stable field structure

selection_signals: a full-width editor preserves a readable writing area
the control has a toolbar, structured content, or contextual panels
editing needs more vertical space than a short scalar field
avoid_when: the task needs only a short plain-text value
a narrow column would compress the writing area or toolbar
custom markup is proposed to recreate an official editor
responsive_considerations: give the editor a full or wide span before reducing toolbar or content readability
keep formatting controls reachable and avoid forcing horizontal precision tasks into narrow columns
accessibility_considerations: retain the editor label and expose formatting actions with discernible names
keep focus order coherent between the toolbar, editor, and any contextual panels
make validation feedback and upload or block insertion failures perceivable without color alone

prefer_when: the workflow needs a constrained, task-specific formatting set
avoid_when: removing controls would block required authoring actions

prefer_when: blocks, mentions, or merge tags are part of authoring and the main writing area stays usable
avoid_when: a panel would obscure the task or appear for irrelevant content

selection_signals: the user must add, preview, inspect, or manage one or more files
file previews or image-editing controls need a wide enough surface
avoid_when: a narrow scalar-field column would compress previews or upload affordances
custom upload cards recreate the native FileUpload interaction
responsive_considerations: let preview grids reduce columns while preserving preview size, filenames, and remove controls
give image editing a full workflow surface rather than embedding it in a cramped group
accessibility_considerations: keep browse, remove, open, download, and editing controls named and keyboard reachable
provide meaningful file names and text alternatives where media meaning is not otherwise available

prefer_when: several visual files benefit from side-by-side recognition
avoid_when: preview tiles become too small to identify or operate

prefer_when: the workflow requires a crop or other image adjustment before submission
avoid_when: the upload is a simple attachment with no editing need

selection_signals: a field selects, creates, edits, or manages related records
relationship labels need search or enough width to remain distinguishable
avoid_when: a relation needs rich per-item fields that belong in a repeater or relation workflow
a custom card is used where native select or relationship controls represent the task
responsive_considerations: preserve readable selected labels and reachable create or edit actions on narrow screens
move a relationship-heavy workflow to its own section, tab, or larger surface when options, details, and actions cannot remain scannable inline
accessibility_considerations: name the relationship and any create or edit action clearly
do not rely on colour or truncation alone to distinguish selected related records
keep result, selected-value, and validation feedback available to keyboard and assistive-technology users

prefer_when: the relationship has enough options that scanning a static list is inefficient
avoid_when: a short stable option set is already easy to scan

prefer_when: the user must resolve a missing or incorrect related record without abandoning the current task
avoid_when: the related-record workflow is too large for an inline action

selection_signals: people need to compare the same decision-relevant facts across many records
identity, state, facts, dates, and actions have a stable scanning order
filters and operations act on a repeatable record list
avoid_when: each record needs materially different rich content that cannot remain comparable in a row
a card or detail-first layout is required by the primary task rather than visual preference
responsive_considerations: retain identity and the state or fact that drives the decision before collapsing secondary information
use an official responsive table layout only while the remaining row still supports peer comparison
do not turn every row into a card merely because the viewport narrows
accessibility_considerations: associate headers with their values and name icon-only controls
keep sorting, filtering, pagination, selected state, grouping, status, and empty-state meaning perceivable without colour alone
preserve keyboard access and visible focus for row and bulk actions

prefer_when: identity, decision-driving state, comparable facts, dates, and actions form the recurring scan path
avoid_when: every available attribute is given equal priority or actions interrupt the data scan

prefer_when: users repeatedly need a named subset such as a status, owner, date range, category, or exception
avoid_when: a filter substitutes for an obvious column, a simple search, or an unexplained hidden result set

prefer_when: state changes the user's decision and needs a concise, scannable label or conventional icon
avoid_when: color alone, including red versus green, is the only way to understand the value

prefer_when: one frequent row action stays direct while secondary, destructive, or uncommon actions would crowd the row
avoid_when: the only common next step is hidden in an ambiguous action menu

prefer_when: users operate on several records at once and the selection scope, consequences, confirmation, and recovery are clear
avoid_when: mixed records make the operation unsafe or the interface implies selection spans pages without explicit support

prefer_when: a shared attribute such as workflow state or date bucket is a useful scan boundary
avoid_when: cross-group comparison matters more than the boundary or collapsed groups would hide discoverable records

prefer_when: an aggregate such as an exception count, total, or average changes a table-level decision
avoid_when: a decorative aggregate competes with row data or its filter, group, or pagination scope is unclear

prefer_when: a large result set needs a visible range, total, and page navigation that preserves comparison context
avoid_when: simpler pagination prevents users from reaching distant pages or understanding their position

prefer_when: the table must distinguish an initial absence from a filter that finds no matches
avoid_when: a filtered empty result invites duplicate creation instead of making active filters and reset available

selection_signals: one record's identity and grouped details matter more than simultaneous column comparison
a desktop row can express an identity-first hierarchy before becoming a mobile stack
secondary detail can move without hiding the state or action that drives the next decision
avoid_when: people must compare the same facts across many peer records
a card-like layout is proposed only for visual novelty rather than a record-centred task
responsive_considerations: reorganize identity, decision-driving state, supporting details, and actions at the breakpoint instead of shrinking desktop columns
reduce content-grid columns before controls or labels become too small
keep the primary action discoverable and secondary details readable when they stack or collapse
accessibility_considerations: keep keyboard access and visible focus for selection, expand/collapse, and row actions across breakpoints
preserve a logical reading order when Split, Stack, or Grid transforms
give visibility and action controls discernible labels and do not rely on colour or layout alone for state

prefer_when: identity, a few primary facts, and a row action form a useful desktop scan line before stacking at a readable breakpoint
avoid_when: long variable content crowds the line or several facts still require cross-record column comparison

prefer_when: related contact, status, or metadata details need one readable vertical unit within a record
avoid_when: independent facts need peer comparison or dense prose hides a common action

prefer_when: grouped peer details benefit from equal tracks while the record remains identity-centred
avoid_when: equal tracks obscure hierarchy or the task needs a standard aligned table

prefer_when: independent identity units remain scannable as responsive record cards at wider breakpoints
avoid_when: cross-record comparison needs persistent column alignment

prefer_when: a short identity or fixed-width fact should preserve its natural width while remaining content uses the available line
avoid_when: growth behaviour truncates decision-critical content or displaces actions

prefer_when: secondary details have a meaningful summary and identity, state, and the recurring action remain visible
avoid_when: collapsed content is needed for the recurring task, selection, error recovery, or a common action

prefer_when: a secondary detail can disappear at a narrow breakpoint while an equivalent identity, state, or action cue remains available
avoid_when: visibility changes remove the only way to understand state or discover an action

selection_signals: repetition makes default spacing unnecessarily slow to scan
adjacent controls remain clearly distinguishable
avoid_when: new or error-prone input needs breathing room
reduced gaps would blur labels, errors, or touch targets
responsive_considerations: restore spacing before labels, errors, or touch targets become crowded on smaller screens
accessibility_considerations: preserve readable error separation and pointer target size
do not use dense spacing to conceal required instructions

prefer_when: repeated low-risk controls remain individually scannable with reduced spacing
avoid_when: the task is new, error-prone, or instruction-heavy

prefer_when: adjacent controls are perceived as one tightly related unit
avoid_when: reduced spacing would blur labels, errors, instructions, or touch targets

prefer_when: the group needs its own hierarchy but less vertical padding
avoid_when: secondary density would weaken the group heading or description

selection_signals: a person needs to notice the current state, investigate a meaningful trend, then act on recent or exceptional records
a small set of headline measures benefits from concise change context before deeper analysis
a chart, table, or filter earns dashboard space only when it supports a recurring operational decision
avoid_when: a custom card system is proposed when a Stats Overview, Chart, or Table widget can express the decision
every available metric receives equal size, prominence, or polling
a chart is chosen for visual novelty without a question, period, or comparable scale
responsive_considerations: start with a readable one-column widget flow, then assign wider spans only to decision-dense trends or activity
keep headline metrics, active filters, and the next actionable exception visible before secondary analytics
reduce widget columns and chart density before shrinking labels, controls, or table actions beyond readable use
accessibility_considerations: pair semantic trend colour with a readable direction and change label; colour alone must not communicate improvement or risk
give widgets concise headings and descriptions that state the decision or time period they support
preserve keyboard access, visible focus, and discernible names for dashboard filters, table actions, and chart controls

prefer_when: a small number of current measures and their direction let a person decide whether to investigate or act
avoid_when: stat tiles merely repeat available data, omit their comparison period, or form an unrelated card system

prefer_when: change over time, distribution, or a comparison between series answers a recurring question that a single metric cannot
avoid_when: the values need exact record-level action first or the chart has no stated decision, period, or meaningful scale

prefer_when: people need a compact queue of recent, exceptional, or actionable records after reading the summary
avoid_when: the dashboard duplicates a full management table without a narrower operational purpose

prefer_when: one shared time period, scope, or named subset changes several widgets and the active scope must remain visible
avoid_when: a local chart or table question can be answered by a scoped control without changing unrelated widgets

prefer_when: a trend or activity widget needs more horizontal space than a concise metric while smaller viewports can stack it
avoid_when: equal spans obscure operational priority or a wide widget leaves no readable mobile fallback
